title: Reduce GPU memory & workspace usage: adaptive activation checkpointing, scratch-buffer pooling, and CUDA arena tuning
author: Asha Patel
body: Motivation: Long-context models and multi-tenant Dedicated hosts are hitting GPU memory headroom and excessive workspace allocations for peak batches. This PR reduces peak GPU memory and temporary workspace by combining three levers: an adaptive activation-checkpointing heuristic (per-layer, cost-aware), a global scratch-buffer pool / reuse path for transient kernel buffers, and CUDA allocator (arena) tuning to reduce fragmentation for long-lived KV caches and occasional big allocations. The description below is intentionally a single continuous string and includes implementation details, benchmarks, and rollout plan. Implementation summary: 1) Adaptive activation checkpointing: introduce a layer-cost estimator that chooses which transformer blocks to checkpoint based on per-layer activation size and FLOP cost, producing a configurable memory/latency pareto. Default policy reduces peak activation memory by ~18% on 8k context for Llama-2-13B-like configs with <8% latency regression. 2) Scratch-buffer pooling: replace per-kernel cudaMalloc/cudaFree transient allocations with a thread-aware arena-backed scratch allocator that reuses temporary buffers across kernels within the same request and across batched inferences where lifetimes permit. This reduces peak transient workspace and cuts per-request allocation stalls. 3) Arena tuning: adjust default cuAllocator arenas and max-bin sizes to trade off footprint vs fragmentation for workloads with large persistent KV caches and intermittent large workspace needs. Also add a telemetry flag (runtime.cu_arena_override) for experiments on Dedicated. Tests and CI: microbenchmarks (gpu_mem_bench) added to verify peak RSS and workspace under synthetic workloads and end-to-end perf tests on perf-canary. Observability: add metrics (runtime.gpu.peak_bytes, runtime.gpu.scratch_reuse_rate) and a short note to the runtime changelog. Migration and rollout: feature gated behind runtime.feature_flags.gpu_mem_savings (off by default), gradual canary rollout to dedicated pools, metrics monitoring for memory regression. Backwards compatibility: no API changes. See release_notes for user-facing summary.

files_changed: runtime/checkpointing.cpp - adaptive per-layer checkpointing logic and config

runtime/arena_manager.cpp - arena tuning and runtime override handling

review_comments: Evan Miller: Nice work — adaptive checkpointing looks promising. Please add more unit coverage around the layer-cost estimator and show output for edge cases (very small layers).
Asha Patel: Added unit tests for tiny/huge layer cases and documented estimator behavior in checkpointing.h (see last two commits).
Priya Nair: I’m concerned about fragmenting long-lived allocations on Dedicated. Can we add a safety cap or diagnostic to fallback to previous arena defaults?
Asha Patel: Added runtime.cu_arena_override and a diagnostic metric runtime.gpu.arena_fallback_count. Default keeps previous thresholds; new tuned values are opt-in per deployment.
Diego Ramos: CI showed sporadic memcheck fail on worker-7; looks like a racy reuse in scratch pool when multiple streams freed buffer simultaneously. Please sync on stream ownership semantics.
Asha Patel: Fixed stream ordering by attaching stream-owner tokens to pool entries and added a stress test in gpu_mem_bench to reproduce. Reran CI.
Evan Miller: Approving after fixes and benchmarks show ~18% peak reduction with acceptable latency tradeoff on our canary workloads.
Priya Nair: LGTM — please watch Dedicated canaries during rollout.
ci_checks: integration (cuda-12, sm86): fail (memcheck flake on worker-7) - rerun requested
perf-canary: pass (bench suite shows peak GPU bytes down ~18% on L2-13B 8k test, scratch reuse rate ~72%)
release_notes: Reduced GPU peak memory by ~15-20% on long-context workloads by enabling an adaptive activation-checkpointing heuristic, adding a scratch buffer pool to reuse transient kernel allocations, and applying tuned CUDA arena defaults. Feature is rollout-gated; enable via runtime.feature_flags.gpu_mem_savings. No API changes. Monitor runtime.gpu.peak_bytes and runtime.gpu.scratch_reuse_rate during rollout.
